In the early 1950s, an irrigation system was planned as part of the Integrated Kamla Project, and King’s canals
were later incorporated into this system. A weir was proposed and constructed across the Kamla River near Jainagar to divert water into the Eastern Kamla Main Canal and the Western Kamla Main Canal systems. The aim was to fully utlize the river’s flow for irrigation Purposes. The project involves Kamla Western Main Canal which Includes a Gross Command Area of 34,953.84 ha, with a CCA of 23,419.08 ha and a discharge capacity of 22.653 cumecs (800 cusecs) and Kamla Eastern Main Canal features a gross command area of 7,410.53 ha and a CCA of 4,965.05 ha with a design capacity of 3.398 cumecs (120 cusecs). The weir is being converted into a barrage and construction of barrage is under progress.

Project Description: The proposed project is Extension, Renovation & Modernization (ERM) of Western Kosi Canal Project in Bihar. A Barrage exists on River Kosi in Nepal with a design discharge of 26,900 cumecs and length of barrage is 1149 m. Eastern and Western Kosi Main canals -take from Kosi Barrage. The total Culturable Command Area (CCA) under this scheme after ERM is 2,15,672 Ha. The proposed ERM aims to rehabilitate and restore the canal infrastructure to address challenges such as drought conditions, sediment flows and the nature of shifting courses. Key interventions include re-lining the main canal, lining of branch canals/ distributaries/ minors/ sub-minors, repairing and upgrading canal structures, and construction of service roads.

Project Description:
The proposed Hathiadah-Durgawati Pumped Storage Project (HDPSP- targeted Installed Capacity 1600 MW) across Durgawati River (a tributary of Karmnasa River) is located near Londa village, Adhaura block, Kaimur District of Bihar, India. . The Upper reservoir is proposed by constructing a bund ring type dam to enclose the area for creating water storage/pondage. The lower reservoir is created by tapping the waterfall of Durgawati River downstream of the Hathiadah-Durgawati water fall by creating a composite rockfill dam with concrete spillway across the river. 
Water will be diverted from the upper reservoir through HRT-Pressure Shaft to an Underground Power House located in between upper and lower reservoir to generate 1600 MW (8 x 200 MW) of power. Being pumped storage project, the water shall be drawn for generation in peak hours from upper reservoir through Pressure Shaft (WCS) and shall be stored in the lower reservoir. The instant proposal is for seeking Invasive S&I permission.

Project Description: The existing SH-97 is substandard horizontal and vertical curves, inadequate sight distance, and several black spots, particularly through the congested built-up areas of Godhila, Patori, Bharwara, and Jale, leading to frequent accidents and traffic delays. To improve safety and traffic flow, the project proposes four bypasses and three realignments after detailed alignment studies. Based on comparative evaluation, Option-3 was selected for the Godhila and Kolhantta Patori bypasses, while Option-2 was chosen for the Bharwara and Jale bypasses. The total project length is 47.905 km, of which 13.280 km comprises bypasses and realignments, while the remaining 34.625 km follows the existing SH-97 through notified Protected Forest. Consequently, diversion of 16.5260 ha of Protected Forest land is unavoidable and has been minimized to the barest extent possible.
